implementation_statement: Group POL-02 Access Control Policy (P06) applies to the PSGCS. The Transmission supplement adds the OT account standard and the station panel password schedule required by the TSA implementation plan.

Named SCADA console and engineering accounts are tied to SYS-G1 identities and created through identity governance with Director of Gas Control approval. Gap: compressor unit control panels at 11 of 41 stations still use shared local accounts whose password mitigations are past the TSA plan schedule (POAM-008), and OT gateway accounts are outside quarterly certification (POAM-002).
evidence: Identity governance export; OT account register; station panel account list

implementation_statement: Joiner, mover, and leaver events from HR drive account creation, change, and disabling in SYS-G1; SCADA local accounts are disabled by the SCADA team from the same ticket within 4 hours.
evidence: Identity governance workflow; termination ticket sample

implementation_statement: Accounts inactive for 35 days are disabled automatically in SYS-G1; the SCADA team runs the same rule monthly on local console accounts.
evidence: Inactivity report; monthly SCADA account review

implementation_statement: The SOC alerts on SCADA and OT DMZ account use outside shift patterns and on new local administrator accounts; the OT desk reviews alerts within 1 hour.
SCADA roles separate controller, senior controller, engineer, and read-only roles; command authority is limited to the controller with the segment assigned on the shift roster.

provider_if_inherited: SYS-G3 Group cloud, network, and data centers
implementation_statement: Flows between zones follow the TSA implementation plan zone model: historian data leaves OT one way through the central and regional DMZs; no business system can open a session into SCADA networks.

Duties are separated between controllers (operate), SCADA engineers (configure), and the Director of Pipeline Cybersecurity (approve security exceptions). Engineers cannot issue control commands in production.
Least privilege is applied to SCADA roles and to OT DMZ servers; engineering rights are granted for change windows only.
Only SCADA engineers may change displays, points, alarm set-points, and station logic; the list of authorized engineers is reviewed quarterly.
Administrators use separate privileged accounts for OT DMZ and SCADA server administration, never their everyday accounts.
Privileged access to OT DMZ and SCADA servers is granted just in time through PAM with session recording.
Privileged sessions and SCADA engineering actions are logged and forwarded to the SIEM through the DMZ log relay.

Engineering workstations and OT DMZ servers lock after 5 failed attempts. Controller consoles do not lock out, so a controller is never locked out during an abnormal condition; the badge-controlled control room compensates (SP 800-82 Rev. 3 OT overlay).
evidence: Lockout settings; control room access logs

implementation_statement: Consoles, engineering workstations, and DMZ servers show the group system use notice at sign-in.
Engineering workstations lock after 15 minutes. Controller consoles do not, because they must stay visible; the room is staffed 24x7 and badge-controlled.

All remote access to the PSGCS goes through the OT remote access gateway with MFA, PAM, and session recording. Gap: the gateway cluster is shared by all three divisions and Integrity Services engineers, so separation depends on gateway policy alone (POAM-001).
evidence: Gateway configuration; access policy; session sample

implementation_statement: Gateway sessions are monitored live by the SOC OT desk; vendor sessions require an approved ticket and are enabled per session.

control_name: Protection of Confidentiality and Integrity Using Encryption
implementation_statement: Remote sessions are encrypted end to end from the user device to the DMZ landing server.
Remote access enters only through the gateway; no other remote access path into the PSGCS exists (verified by the 2026 firewall review).
No wireless networks inside SCADA zones; station wireless for maintenance laptops is on a separate isolated network.
External systems (IDP, vendor portals) may receive PSGCS data only through approved exports from SYS-G6; no external system connects to SCADA.
Group security awareness and training policy and procedures (POL-05).
All workforce complete annual awareness training and quarterly phishing exercises.
Training covers insider threat indicators and reporting.

Controllers, SCADA engineers, and station technicians take role-based OT security training each year. Gap: controller training does not cover cyber-caused abnormal operating conditions such as false SCADA data or loss of SCADA integrity (192.631(h)(1); POAM-011).
Group logging standard under POL-01.
Logged events for SCADA servers, OT DMZ servers, firewalls, and the gateway are defined in the OT logging profile.
Records include time, source, user, action, and result; SCADA command logs include the console and the point.

control_name: Audit Record Review, Analysis, and Reporting
implementation_statement: The SOC OT desk reviews OT alerts continuously. Gap: communications between OT and external systems are not yet compared with a documented baseline at 4 external connections (III.D.2.b; POAM-003).
SIEM correlation and SOAR playbooks automate review and triage.
OT and IT logs are correlated in one SIEM so an IT intrusion moving toward OT is visible.
SCADA hosts and DMZ servers use internal time servers synchronized to GPS clocks at both gas control centers.
Logs forwarded to the SIEM are write-protected and access is limited to SOC roles.
The TSA implementation plan sets 1-year retention for OT security logs. Gap: the two regional OT DMZ firewalls keep 90 days locally and forward only summary events (POAM-013).
SCADA, DMZ, and gateway components generate the events in the OT logging profile.
Group assessment policy (POL-01 4.9) and the TSA Cybersecurity Assessment Plan.

The TSA-approved assessment plan schedules 96 measures for 2026-2027 and group internal audit assesses common controls yearly. Gaps: the architecture design review lapsed on 2026-05-20, and only 22% of scheduled measures had been assessed by 2026-08-28 (POAM-009).

Common controls are assessed by group internal audit; the architecture design review is performed by an outside firm, not by the Integrity Services OT Assessment Practice, to keep it independent of the group.
Interconnections with SYS-T4, SYS-T5, SYS-G6, and SYS-E1 are documented in the TSA plan zone model and an interconnection register.
One POA&M tracks P07 findings, TSA plan measures, and 192.631 records gaps; the Cybersecurity Coordinator reviews it monthly.

responsible_role: Group CISO with the Gas Transmission president
implementation_statement: Internal authorization to operate with conditions (SSP section 4.2).
Continuous monitoring through the SOC OT desk, monthly vulnerability reports, and the assessment schedule.
Annual penetration test of the IT systems that border OT and of SYS-T5; a purple team exercise against the central DMZ was run in 2025-11.
evidence: Penetration test report 2026-03; purple team report 2025-11

implementation_statement: Internal connections inside SCADA zones (consoles, hosts, historians, station links) are documented in the zone diagram and reviewed after every change.
Group configuration management standard; Transmission management of change procedure for OT.
Baseline configurations for SCADA hosts, consoles, DMZ servers, and station control systems are kept in the OT configuration repository.
The last two approved configurations are kept offline for rollback.

OT changes go through management of change with Gas Control sign-off. Gap: leak-detection model threshold changes and 3 station control upgrades in 2026-03 were made without full control room change coordination or complete point-to-point records (192.631(c)(2), (f); POAM-010).
Security impact analysis is part of each OT change request; changes are tested on the SCADA test system first.
Only authorized engineers can change production SCADA; changes are pushed from the engineering workstation in change windows.

provider_if_inherited: SYS-G3 Group cloud, network, and data centers
implementation_statement: Hardening baselines (CIS-based for Windows servers; vendor guides for SCADA) are applied and checked monthly.
Unneeded services and ports are disabled on hosts and consoles; USB ports are disabled on consoles.
Application allowlisting runs on consoles, engineering workstations, and DMZ servers; macros cannot run.
The OT asset inventory is built from passive monitoring and site surveys and covers 36 of 41 stations automatically; the other 5 are surveyed manually each quarter.
The inventory is updated with each change and each new station.
Users cannot install software; installs go through the software catalog and, for OT, through MOC.
Group contingency planning policy (POL-03) and the Transmission business continuity standard.

The contingency plan covers loss of SCADA (failover and manual operation) and is integrated with the emergency plan. Gap: it assumes business IT returns within 24 hours and its manual fallback for nominations and measurement has only been exercised for 8 hours (POAM-006).
The contingency plan is coordinated with the 192.615 emergency plan and the 192.605 manual.
Gas control and emergency response resume within 1 hour at the Backup Gas Control Center.
Controllers train on failover and manual operation each year.
Backup SCADA is tested yearly and the internal communication plan for manual operation is tested yearly. Gap: business-critical services have not been tested beyond 8 hours (POAM-006).

implementation_statement: Offline SCADA backups are stored at the other gas control center; cloud backups go to the immutable vault in provider B.
The Backup Gas Control Center in Louisiana can run the whole system.

provider_if_inherited: SYS-G3 Group cloud, network, and data centers

implementation_statement: SCADA communications use private microwave and MPLS with satellite backup at every compressor station.

provider_if_inherited: SYS-G3 Group cloud, network, and data centers
implementation_statement: SCADA hosts and historians are backed up offline monthly and before every change; backups are scanned and hashed when made and before restore.
A bare-metal restore of a SCADA host is tested each year on the test system.
Recovery procedures restore SCADA, then station communication, then historians, with point-to-point checks for any changed point.

baseline: Not in baseline (SP 800-82 Rev. 3 OT overlay addition)
implementation_statement: On loss of SCADA communication, station control systems hold the last setpoints and hardwired emergency shutdown remains available (safe mode).
Group identification and authentication standard (POL-02).
Users are uniquely identified: SYS-G1 identities for business and gateway access; named local SCADA accounts tied to SYS-G1 identifiers on consoles.
Privileged access through the gateway and PAM requires phishing-resistant MFA.

Non-privileged remote access requires MFA. Controller consoles in the control room use passwords plus badge-controlled room access as the compensating control the SD allows for control room workstations under Part 192.
Station and field devices are identified by network address and allowlisted at station firewalls; legacy serial protocols cannot authenticate devices, and network isolation compensates.
Identifiers are assigned through identity governance and never reused.

Memorized secrets follow the reset schedule in the TSA implementation plan. Gap: mitigations for unit control panels that cannot be reset on schedule are overdue at 11 of 41 stations, and no amendment request was filed (III.C.1.b; VI.B; POAM-008).
Password rules follow NIST SP 800-63B; breached-password screening is enforced in SYS-G1 and on SCADA local accounts.
Group incident response policy (POL-03) and the Transmission Cybersecurity Incident Response Plan.
Positions named in the CIRP train each year before the exercise.
The CIRP exercise on 2026-04-22 tested containment and IT/OT isolation (III.F.1.a and d). Gap: no exercise has combined the shutdown decision with the cross-division notification matrix (POAM-004).
Incident handling follows the CIRP and the P08 runbook, including memory capture before power-off and labeling of infected equipment.
SOAR playbooks drive standardized response steps.
Incidents are tracked in the SOC case system with the identification time for the 72-hour CISA clock.

Cybersecurity incidents are reported to CISA within 72 hours of identification (SD 01G II.C). Gap: the reporting procedure does not cover FERC 260.9 reports, SSI disclosure reports, or client notices (POAM-005).
The CIRP names responsible positions and resources and is updated yearly.
Maintenance of SCADA and station control systems follows the O&M manual and MOC.
Nonlocal maintenance happens only through gateway sessions with MFA and recording.
Vendor technicians on site are escorted; their laptops are scanned at the station before connection.
Removable media in control rooms and stations is limited to scanned, numbered media.
Retired SCADA drives are sanitized under NIST SP 800-88 Rev. 2 and certificates kept.
Personal and unscanned media are prohibited on OT systems.
Access to gas control centers and stations is authorized by role.
Badge and PIN at control rooms; badge at stations; video at both.
Physical access events at control rooms and stations feed the SIEM.
Both gas control centers have UPS and generators tested monthly.
Group planning policy; Transmission supplement.
This SSP, aligned with the TSA implementation plan.
Rules of behavior (POL-05) acknowledged yearly; controllers also acknowledge the control room rules.
The OT security architecture follows the TSA plan zone model and SP 800-82 Rev. 3.
Group information security program plan.
Group CISO leads the program; the Director of Pipeline Cybersecurity is the TSA Cybersecurity Coordinator with alternates.
Group risk management strategy and acceptance authority (POL-01 4.4).
Background checks for controllers, SCADA engineers, and gateway users; the Cybersecurity Coordinator holds U.S. citizenship as SD 01G requires.
Termination disables SYS-G1 access within 4 hours; SCADA local accounts and shared panel passwords known to the person are changed (III.C.4.b).
Vendor and integrator personnel requirements are in contracts; Integrity Services engineers follow the same rules under the intercompany agreement.
PSGCS information is categorized (SSP section 6); TSA plan content is SSI.
Annual risk analysis (P01) covers the PSGCS and its business dependencies.
Passive vulnerability identification for OT and authenticated scans of DMZ servers monthly; KEV entries are flagged.
Critical Cyber Systems are identified in the TSA implementation plan (14 systems).
OT purchases include security requirements from the group OT procurement language.
External services that hold PSGCS data are reviewed yearly. Gap: the IDP (intercompany) holds Transmission SSI without SSI controls (POAM-019).
The SCADA vendor and integrators follow the MOC and deliver changes to the test system first.
Vendor releases are tested on the SCADA test system with security checks before production.
Unsupported components are tracked. Gap: 14 station HMIs run an unsupported operating system without the documented mitigations the TSA plan requires (III.E.3; POAM-012).

EDR on DMZ servers and engineering workstations; allowlisting on consoles.
Passive OT monitoring at both gas control centers and 36 of 41 stations. Gap: the 5 stations added or rebuilt since 2025 have no sensor (POAM-003).

Threat intelligence from CISA, TSA, and the sector information sharing center is triaged by the OT desk.
File integrity monitoring on SCADA hosts and hash checks on station logic against the offline repository.

Group supply chain risk management plan covers SCADA and station control vendors.
Supply chain controls in OT contracts (notice of vulnerabilities, signed updates).
Yearly supplier assessments for the SCADA vendor, station control vendors, and carriers.
Station control spare parts are bought from authorized channels and checked before installation.
